questions.q: What is the Equipment Checkout application's critical path, as this lab defines it?
options: A list of every field on the request table, regardless of workflow
The request-approval-availability-check sequence that absolutely has to keep working through future changes to the application
Only the Script Include's code, with no connection to the UI
The order in which the application's tables were originally created
questions.explain: The critical path is the one end-to-end sequence — employee request, manager approval, availability enforcement — that this lab designs ATF coverage for.

questions.q: Why does the lab's UI Test need two separate Impersonate User steps?
options: Because the critical path involves two different people, an employee and their manager, acting in sequence, and each should be tested as that real role
Because Impersonate User steps have no real effect on which UI Policies apply
Because a single impersonated user cannot submit more than one form in a Test
Because ATF requires every UI Test to impersonate exactly two users regardless of scenario
questions.explain: Testing as an admin instead of the real employee and manager roles would bypass the same UI Policies and ACLs those roles actually encounter.

questions.q: What does the lab's server-side Test specifically validate?
options: That EquipmentAvailabilityChecker.isEquipmentAvailable() returns false for equipment that is already checked out
That the request form's UI Policy hides the correct field for employees
That the Test Suite itself is scheduled correctly
That the manager's approval button is visible on the form
questions.explain: The server-side Test creates a Checked Out request directly, then calls the Script Include method and checks its return value.

questions.q: Why are the UI Test and server-side Test grouped into a single Test Suite rather than left as two separate, unrelated Tests?
options: Because a UI Test cannot be scheduled unless it is grouped with a server-side Test
Because grouping removes the need for the server-side Test's verification step
So they report one combined result for the whole critical path and can be scheduled to run together automatically
Because ATF does not allow more than one Test to exist for the same application
questions.explain: The Test Suite, "Equipment Checkout Regression," is this lab's mechanism for coordinated, scheduled coverage of the critical path.

questions.q: What happens if a future Business Rule change breaks the availability check, once this lab's Suite is scheduled nightly?
options: The very next nightly run surfaces it as a failed Test, ready to investigate before a real employee is affected
Nothing — scheduled Suites only report successes, never failures
The failure is only visible if someone happens to manually open the Test record that week
The Script Include is automatically reverted to its previous version
questions.explain: That's the whole point of Scheduled Test Execution from Lesson 15 — catching the regression the next night, not weeks later.
